target.title: fix(text): strip MiniMax marker from channel replies
target.body: Closes #105113 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where MiniMax replies could expose the `[e~[` message-end marker in channel messages, making otherwise valid responses appear corrupted. ## Why This Change Was Made The shared model-special-token sanitizer now recognizes only this exact MiniMax control token. It keeps the existing code-region protection intact, so inline and fenced examples of the marker remain visible, while ordinary bracket text is unchanged. ## User Impact Users receive clean MiniMax replies through Telegram and every other delivery path that uses the shared assistant-visible-text sanitizer. ## Evidence - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.test.ts` (114 tests passed) - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-utils.strip-model-special-tokens.test.ts` (5 tests passed) - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/telegram-outbound.test.ts` (15 tests passed) - `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/shared/text/model-special-tokens.ts src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-utils.strip-model-special-tokens.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/telegram-outbound.test.ts` - `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local` (clean; no accepted/actionable findings) - Blacksmith Testbox-through-Crabbox is unavailable in this environment because it is not authenticated to the `openclaw` organization. The focused tests above are an explicitly reported local fallback; remote build and GitHub CI remain pending. Tested commit: `d140ff501333a0864d406cba7f289fdec76d228a` Runtime model: `minimax/MiniMax-M3` I sent a Telegram message requesting a `read` of the workspace `package.json`. The final reply was delivered normally and does not contain the trailing MiniMax `[e~[` marker. *Redacted Telegram screenshot:*
